answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with earned standing: a new identity starts with almost no privileges and only gains weight by doing useful, verified work over time. Attackers can wander in with a thousand fresh accounts, but each one is as light as shale dust until it proves itself. The cost is time, not money: a reputation built slowly is like quartz, hard to fake quickly and easy to spot when hollow. A farm of brand-new accounts can shout, but it cannot borrow the trust that only a long, honest record earns.
